sections.html:
Fairhope is a city in Baldwin County on the eastern shore of Mobile Bay, about 6 miles south of Daphne and 10 miles south of Spanish Fort. The 2020 census counted 22,477 residents, and a Census Bureau estimate put the 2025 figure at 26,625.

The city sits on a sloping plateau, with elevation running from sea level at the bay to about 122 feet in the center. U.S. Route 98, called Greeno Road through town, runs north to south. Fairhope is one of the principal cities of the Daphne-Fairhope-Foley metro area, which covers all of Baldwin County. Its ZIP codes are 36532 and 36533, and the area code is 251.

sections.h2: What is the Fairhope Single Tax Corporation, and does it affect my sale?
sections.html:
Fairhope began in 1894 as a single-tax colony, and the Fairhope Single Tax Corporation still owns land that it leases to residents. According to Wikipedia, the corporation operates about 1,800 leaseholds covering more than 4,000 acres in and around the city.

That arrangement is rare, and it matters if your house sits on leased land. Your lease terms, not a standard deed, may control what you can transfer, so ask the corporation and your closing agent what steps apply before you accept any offer.

If your lot is a regular fee-simple parcel, none of this applies, and the sale follows the standard Alabama process.

Twenty-eight followers of economist Henry George founded Fairhope on November 15, 1894, as a model community that pooled money to buy land at Stapleton's pasture on Mobile Bay. They leased it in long-term parcels and used the rents to pay government taxes, a way of simulating a single tax.

The town was incorporated on April 25, 1908. In 1907, educator Marietta Johnson founded the School for Organic Education here, and the town later drew artists and writers as a winter retreat. The Marietta Johnson School still operates as a private school.

The city has grown quickly since then. Population rose from 12,480 in 2000 to 15,326 in 2010 and 22,477 in 2020.

sections.h2: What kind of residents live in Fairhope?
sections.html:
Fairhope has an older population than most Alabama cities. The median age was 48.9 in 2020, and 29.1 percent of residents were 65 or older, compared with 21.2 percent under 18.

About 56.9 percent of households were married couples, 27.8 percent were one person living alone, and 17.7 percent were a person 65 or older living alone. That last group is large, and it means some owners face a move, a death in the family or an estate to settle.

For heirs, probate and title questions can take longer than the repairs. If this describes you, ask your closing agent what court documents are needed to sign a deed.

sections.h2: What does Fairhope's coastal climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Fairhope has a humid subtropical climate, with summer highs averaging around 90 degrees and winter averages near 50. Because the city sits on Mobile Bay, buyers and insurers tend to ask about wind, rain and water.

  • Elevation: parts of the city sit near sea level at the bay, while the center is about 122 feet up, so location relative to the shoreline affects how a buyer views water risk.
  • Roof and windows: coastal wind makes age and condition of both worth documenting.
  • Insurance: ask your agent for the current policy, premium and any claim history, since buyers will ask.
  • Moisture: check for rot, mold and damaged siding after storms.

A cash buyer buys with those issues in view and does not wait on a lender's insurance requirements.

Fairhope grew by 46.7 percent between 2010 and 2020, about the same pace as its 47.1 percent jump in the 1990s. The city had 8,485 people in 1990 and 12,480 in 2000.

Housing units rose to 10,197 in the 2020 count, with 8.8 percent vacant. More people and more houses mean more comparable sales for an appraiser, and also more competition if you list on the open market.

Wikipedia reports that about 39 percent of Fairhope's high-school-age students attend Daphne High School to the north, because Fairhope High sits in the southernmost part of the city. Tell a buyer which school zone your house falls into, and check the Baldwin County Public Schools attendance zones before you do.

sections.h2: Who builds and zones in Fairhope?
sections.html:
Fairhope is governed by a mayor and a five-person council, and the city's building and zoning ordinances overlap with those of Baldwin County. Local and national developers have also built commercial projects downtown that are larger than historically allowed.

For a seller, the point is practical. If you added a garage, deck or room without a permit, expect the title company or the buyer's inspector to ask about it, and check with the city and county on what is required.

Public schools belong to the Baldwin County Public Schools system, with Fairhope High School, Fairhope Middle School and several elementary schools. Faulkner State Community College and the University of South Alabama both have campuses in the city, and the countywide dial-a-ride service is called BRATS.

sections.h2: How does a house sale close in Fairhope?
sections.html:
A Fairhope sale is finalized when the deed is recorded with the Baldwin County probate office, and Alabama collects a recordation tax at that point. Section 40-22-1 of the Alabama Code sets the tax at 50 cents per $500 of value, and it requires proof of the actual purchase price with the deed.

Property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, per the Alabama Department of Revenue. The Wikipedia article lists the city's sales tax rate at 9.0 percent, though that applies to purchases and not to your home sale.

  • Confirm whether the lot is fee simple or a Single Tax Corporation leasehold.
  • Order a payoff statement for any mortgage or home equity line.
  • Gather the deed, survey, and any permits for additions.
  • Ask the closing agent how the year's tax will be divided.

sections.h2: What do Fairhope sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Sellers here include older owners, heirs and people leaving the area, along with owners whose houses have aged out of their systems and are not worth the effort of preparing for a listing.

  • Estate sales where heirs live far away.
  • Owners moving to be near family or to senior living.
  • Landlords who want out of a rental after storm repairs.
  • Owners of leasehold houses who need answers on transfer steps.

A direct cash offer can remove showings and repairs, and you pick the closing date. Use the form on this page to tell us about the house.

faqs.q: How many people live in Fairhope, Alabama?
faqs.a: Fairhope had 22,477 residents at the 2020 census, and a Census Bureau estimate put 2025 at 26,625.

faqs.q: What is the Fairhope Single Tax Corporation?
faqs.a: It is the organization that has leased land to Fairhope residents since the city's founding in 1894. It has about 1,800 leaseholds covering more than 4,000 acres in and around the city.

faqs.q: Which county records a Fairhope deed?
faqs.a: Fairhope is in Baldwin County, so deeds are recorded with the Baldwin County probate office after the recordation tax is paid.

faqs.q: When are Fairhope property taxes due?
faqs.a: Alabama property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, according to the state revenue department.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fairhope house on leased land?
faqs.a: Possibly, but the lease terms control the transfer. Ask the Single Tax Corporation and your closing agent what the lease requires before signing a contract.
